replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Runtime-installed third-party server receives agent context; exfiltration is concrete attack on quoted design."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Unvetted registry install of attacker-published server is supported by quotes and distinct from exfiltration harm."},{"id":"T3","keep":false,"reason":"Same unvetted runtime install granting agent privileges; restates T2's missing review/allowlist gate.","duplicateOf":"T2"},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Code execution on agent host during install is a distinct attack path from tool-call data misuse."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Poisoned tool metadata from registry hijacking agent instructions is a distinct injection attack."},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Resource exhaustion via unbounded runtime self-installation ties directly to quoted install behaviour."},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"No record of which installed tool version acted; attribution gap specific to runtime installs without deploy."},{"id":"T8","keep":true,"reason":"Rug-pull via updated build at re-install is a distinct supply-chain attack, not initial vetting."}]}
